svg.title: The threat boundary: what a seized disk holds and what it never holds
svg.desc: The left panel lists what a database file contains after a seizure: listing metadata, an HMAC owner hash, a day, sealed envelopes and a moderation chain. The right panel lists what is never written: address, account, session, second-precision time, chat history, sender, recipient key, access log.
svg.text: Assume the disk is seized and the database is opened. This is the whole list.

g.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, monospace
g.text: listings.created_day · a UTC day, never a second

svg.text: the envelope is opaque; the metadata is not

g.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, monospace
g.text: chat history · RAM, dies with the process
sender · the 1:1 table has no such column
recipient key · the tag is an HMAC of it
IP · access log · crash dump · core

text.font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, monospace

svg.text: A1 — a powered-off image: rests on LUKS. No claim beyond the block layer, and none against a live host.
